column4: Continue the reference: identical camera and doll wrist, but now the librarian's fingers have pulled away to the LEFT, pinching the tiny end of nothing, held a little way from the ring, leaving the doll's wrist ring plain and empty. No threads drawn, no text.

Same dark background and horizontal framing. On the left a living librarian's hand with a white cuff, on the right the porcelain doll's hand with ball joints and a wrist ring, both reaching toward each other horizontally across the center and almost touching, a small clear gap of about a finger's width between the fingertips. Five fingers on each hand. No threads, no text.

Continue the reference: identical camera and framing, but now her eye is OPEN: a round iris of orange with a black pupil and one small paper-white highlight, lashes lifted, the look steady and a little astonished. Same face, hair, flower ornament. No text.

Wide view of the same cathedral nave from the first reference, seen from the stage end. At the left-center on the stone floor, a living librarian (third reference) stands facing a small porcelain maid doll (second reference), both holding one hand out toward each other horizontally, about to touch. On the right wall of the nave a small puppet-theater cell from the last reference shows a doll's arm stretching out toward the left. At the far right edge, a large bare porcelain hand enters horizontally from outside the frame, reaching left. No strings or threads. No text.
